title: Proactive surge isolation and staged bounce procedure
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
This ticket codifies an operational playbook and a small set of tactical fixes for handling cross-region surge-induced instability that manifests as prolonged tail latency + proxy connection churn in Hosted and Dedicated fleets. The goal is an automated, controlled isolation of surge traffic, a staged application-level 'bounce' (process restart/sidecar reload) sequence for impacted hosts, and guaranteed KV-cache reconciliation to avoid request loss or model context corruption for multi-tenant workloads.

Why now:
- Multiple customers reported generation truncation and inconsistent outputs during region-level spikes where edge proxies rapidly cycled connections.
- Mitigations so far (broad evacuations and blunt circuit breakers) are high-impact for customers. We need a lower-blast-radius orchestration sequence that preserves operator control.

Scope:
- Diagnostics and instrumentation additions (marker events, dashboards)
- A staged isolation + weighted-split traffic plan (per-tenant) implemented in the routing plane
- Safe bounce sequence for inference workers and edge proxy sidecars with KV snapshot + validation steps
- Clear comms templates and rollback criteria for Customer Success and Support
- Automated tests and a rehearsal runbook for fire drills

Non-goals:
- Full redesign of routing (we keep current route abstraction).
- Major runtime kernel changes; this ticket includes only a targeted hotfix to prevent KV desync during rapid reconnects.

Runbook (operator-facing):
Phase 0 — Detect and Triage:
1) Detection triggers: 3x increase in p99 latency across >10% hosts in region OR >2% connection churn rate in edge-proxy logs for 10 minutes.
2) Initial checks: health of placement service, edge-proxy error rates (503/504), model-serving tail latencies, KV-applier lag, and leader lease stability. Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/CRR/region-health, Query snippets in Confluence.
3) Escalation: page on-call infra + SRE lead, notify CS/Account team if affected customers are in the incident list.

Phase 1 — Soft Isolation (per-tenant):
1) Create a shadow route that receives 0% traffic initially.
2) For tenants impacted, incrementally shift traffic to the shadow route using weighted-splits: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 3 minutes with health checks at each step. Purpose: verify behavior on an isolated backend variant (no cache priming) before wider action.
3) If errors spike by >10% from baseline, immediately revert weight by 1 step and mark host-set for deeper investigation.

Phase 2 — Controlled Bounce Sequence:
1) For host-sets failing isolation checks, perform the following in parallel per host but staggered across the AZ to protect capacity: a) drain inbound queue for 30s, b) snapshot KV-cache to s3://kv-snapshots/<region>/<host>/<ts>, c) restart proxy sidecar with environment flag PROXY_SAFE_RELOAD=true, d) run post-start KV-validate job to compare snapshot checksums.
2) If KV mismatch is detected, automatically quiesce the host and kick off a targeted cache-repopulation job that sources from the live primaries.
3) After successful validation, reintroduce the host to the load balancer at 10% weight and ramp to 100% over 6 minutes with metrics gating.

Phase 3 — Global Traffic Rebalancing and Warm Standby Activation:
1) If region-level deterioration continues after staged bounces, enable warm-standby regions using policy: tenant-priority > enterprise -> midmarket -> free-tier. 2) Use tenant-aware weighted-slicing to move only high-priority tenants first. 3) When migrating, preserve model version pinning and KV-state read-only mode until validation passes.

Rollback criteria:
- Any stage where 5xx rates increase >20% above pre-incident baseline OR token truncation detected in more than 3% of requests for a tenant -> rollback to previous traffic weights and abort host reintroduction.

Telemetry and observability additions (implementation notes):
- Emit RUNBOOK_MARKER event for each step with fields: step_name, host, tenant_slice, pre_metrics (p95, p99, error_rate). Implement as structured logs to Snowplow.
- Add KV snapshot checksum metric and a KV-repopulate-duration histogram.
- Dashboard panels: per-tenant weight, per-host KV-checksum-status, proxy-reload-duration, and customer-visible error rate.

Customer communications:
- Templates stored at Confluence: /docs/incidents/CRR/communications-template. Customer Success will use two templates: 1) initial notice (we are investigating + mitigation underway), 2) post-incident summary with actions and ETA for permanent fix.

Engineering tasks (concrete):
- ENG-765433: Add RUNBOOK_MARKER structured logging to routing-proxy (owner: Ravi).
- ENG-765434: Implement KV snapshot + checksum endpoint on host-agent (owner: Mei Chen).
- ENG-765435: Routing control API: weighted-split per-tenant with ramping parameters (owner: Samir Patel).
- ENG-765436: Postmortem automation: capture runbook markers into incident timeline (owner: SRE team).

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook validated in a staged rehearsal with synthetic tenants without impacting production customers.
- Metrics emitted for each RUNBOOK_MARKER and visible in dashboards.
- No token loss observed for demo tenant during a full run.
- Customer comms template reviewed and approved by Support and Legal.

Notes and tradeoffs:
- We opted for per-tenant weighted-splits rather than whole-region cutovers to reduce blast radius, at the cost of more complex orchestration.
- The snapshot-and-validate approach adds ~200ms overhead to host-side snapshotting; we believe this is acceptable during incident windows because it prevents KV divergence.
